bull_bear.body: Prioritizing core business CAPEX, disciplined R&D in EV and energy tech, 100% acquisition of Excel in Q2FY27, no dividend policy mentioned, EV business funded via parent support until profitability
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Commodity price volatility, EV market competition and funding constraints, geopolitical disruption in exports, delayed IPO timing due to market volatility, integration risks from new product launches
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, disciplined, execution-focused; strong emphasis on profitability over volume in core, transparent on EV losses, optimistic on international and tech innovation, cautious on macro
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: 1) 650kVA genset is fully in-house engine — rare in Indian genset market; 2) Rare-earth-free EV motors piloted — potential cost and supply chain advantage; 3) 350 new retailers onboarded with 3,000 target by FY27 — retail network scaling is a hidden margin lever; 4) Defense engine repowering trucks — strategic entry into defense supply chain
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "Disciplined capital allocation towards high-potential growth opportunities" is the stated Greaves.Next principle; "Priority on execution discipline, portfolio mix optimization and capital efficiency".
- GEML rights issue is stated two different ways in the same deck: the Greaves.Next slide says "Fully subscribed to the rights issue of ₹331 Cr for GEML", while the GEML slide says "Successfully raised ₹530 Cr through a fully subscribed Rights issue, with participation from all shareholders in their proportion".
- Invested ₹50 Cr in GFL; GFL slide states "Equity: Raised 50 Cr from GCL increasing the networth to ₹153 Cr".
- "Focused on sustained organic growth, complemented by selective inorganic opportunities".
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Leadership in India's diesel three-wheeler segment with domestic market share improved to ~60% (Source: Vahaan sewa)
- Fuel-agnostic powertrain strategy (diesel, CNG, petrol, hydrogen concepts) enabling competitiveness across urban and rural/cargo segments
- 165+ year engineering legacy and manufacturing/validation capability underpinning international partnerships (e.g. Ligier for Euro V+ compliant microcar engines in Europe)
- Wide distribution and service network: 200+ distributors, 20,000+ mechanics and 7,000+ retailers supporting the aftermarket business
- Shift toward high-margin recurring revenue (spares, AMCs, service contracts) in Energy Solutions reducing cyclicality
- Full OBD-IIB certification across diesel & CNG powertrain lineup (effective April 1, 2025) supporting regulatory compliance ahead of customer launches
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Technology transition risk — Industry-wide shift toward cleaner fuels, electric mobility and emerging technologies (alternate fuels, battery storage, hybrid/gas-based solutions, software-led systems) could reduce demand for the Company's conventional (diesel/petrol/CNG) product lines.
- Demand and execution risk — Demand is linked to macroeconomic conditions, customer capex cycles and infrastructure activity; delays in industrial/infrastructure capex, regulatory-led transitions, or demand normalisation in certain segments may impact volumes.
- Competitive intensity — Operates in competitive markets across businesses; pricing pressure, low-cost offerings and margin expectations in contracts may impact profitability and market position.
- Regulatory and policy risk — Businesses are subject to evolving regulatory requirements including emission norms, fuel policies, EV incentive structures and product compliance standards; policy changes on diesel usage, alternate fuels or emission standards could affect demand and cost structures.
- Global macroeconomic risk — Geopolitical tensions, inflationary pressures, interest rate movements, currency fluctuations and global trade uncertainties may affect demand, export performance and supply chain stability.
- Supply chain and input cost risk — Exposure to commodity price volatility, energy/fuel cost fluctuations and supply chain disruptions from geopolitical developments and trade barriers; dependence on certain imported components poses risk until localisation improves.
- Technology and capability risk — Rapid advancements across electric powertrains, components and engineering technologies require continuous investment in R&D, talent and capabilities to remain competitive.
- Compliance risk (export markets) — Export-oriented businesses are subject to international standards and certification requirements; regulatory changes or non-compliance could impact market access and operations.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Energy Solutions: 20% YoY growth, 35% aftermarket growth, 650kVA in-house engine launched; Mobility Solutions: 16% YoY growth, 63% market share in diesel 3-wheelers, Euro V+ exports to Ligier (Europe); Industrial Solutions: 15% YoY growth, defense and agri OEM wins; Excel Controlinkage: Double-digit domestic growth, export recovery underway, 100% acquisition planned in Q2FY27
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Founded in 1859 and described as one of India's oldest engineering companies, with "Over 165 years of expertise in engineering and product development"; recognised as Best Governed Company (Listed Segment - Emerging Category) at the 25th ICSI National Awards for Excellence in Corporate Governance.
- Differentiation framed as: Complete Engineering Solutions Provider with "adaptable & sustainable engine platforms across fuel types", an "Integrated Mobility Ecosystem - Building synergies across Engineering + EV manufacturing + Retail + Finance + Tech Services", Partner-of-Choice OEM relationships and a wide pan-India distribution footprint.
- Structure splits Core Businesses (B2B: Energy Solutions, Industrial Solutions, Mobility Solutions) from Investee Businesses (B2C: Greaves Electric Mobility Ltd for EV Mobility, Greaves Finance Ltd for EV Financing).
- International business described as "a core growth engine, contributing a double-digit share across GCL and Excel"; INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS REVENUE 13% (FY26), and "International business revenue share on track at 13% of Core business sales".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [M&A history] Acquired Ampere Vehicles in 2019 (last-mile e-Mobility, later renamed Greaves Electric Mobility Ltd) and Excel Controlinkage in 2023 for "strategic expansion into advanced motion-control solutions".
- [Regulation as demand driver] Deck cites "STRINGENT EMISSION AND FUEL REGULATIONS like BS VII" and India's Viksit Bharat / infrastructure push as opportunity drivers; capital goods sector said to contribute ~1.9% of GDP.
- [Partnerships] Long-standing OEM ties include Piaggio Group for India business (1998) and marquee OEM Ligier; GEML expanded financing tie-ups with AU Small Finance Bank, V-Pay Finance and Kosh Finance.
- [Awards] Greaves Technologies awarded Inspirational Runner-up by Daimler India Commercial Vehicles (Indirect Procurement); SBDO Global Supplier Quality Award; Ampere Nexus won Electric Scooter of the Year (2025) and Magnus G-Max won "Family Scooter of the Year" at Times Drive Auto Summit 2026.
- [Entity scope] GEML Consolidated includes MLR Auto Ltd. and Bestway Agencies Pvt. Ltd.; GCL Consolidated figures are "Post knocking-off Inter-Company adjustments"; Core Businesses = Energy + Mobility + Industrial Solutions.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Greaves Cotton Limited manufactures diesel, gasoline, petrol and CNG engines, pump sets, gensets, farm equipment and industrial engines, delivering precision powertrain and power solutions for automotive, agriculture, marine, construction and railway customers. Under its Greaves.Next strategic roadmap the Company is organised around Energy Solutions (gensets and lifecycle power services), Mobility Solutions (auto engines and aftermarket retail) and Industrial Solutions, while investee businesses Greaves Electric Mobility Limited (electric 2W/3W) and Greaves Finance Limited (EV-focused NBFC lending) extend its reach into consumer-facing segments.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Energy Solutions:** Gensets, Annual Maintenance Contracts (AMCs), IoT-enabled power monitoring, Lithium-ion battery backup solutions, Spares distribution
- **Auto Engines:** Diesel three-wheeler (3W) engines, CNG powertrains, Petrol engines, Euro V+ 499cc microcar diesel engines, Hydrogen engine concepts (showcased), Lightweight bi-fuel CNG engines
- **Aftermarket Retail:** Multi-brand spares & lubricants, Engineered components for CV & Construction Equipment, EV Components
- **Industrial Solutions:** Industrial engines, Non-auto engines, Farm equipment, Marine engines, Firefighting equipment
business.title: Products & brands

business.body:
- Greaves Finance Limited (GFL) — subsidiary: Wholly owned (100%) subsidiary; NBFC engaged in Retail Vehicle Financing for electric 2-wheeler & 3-wheeler purchasers and lease financing for last-mile delivery/service aggregators; also a registered IRDAI corporate agent for composite corporate insurance agency business.
- Greaves Technologies Limited (GTL) — subsidiary: Wholly owned (100%) subsidiary providing engineering services to OEMs for development and maintenance of engines, plant, machinery & equipment.
- Greaves Electric Mobility Limited (GEML) — subsidiary: Material subsidiary (62.48% holding) engaged in designing and manufacturing electric vehicles (E2W/E3W).
- Bestway Agencies Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned (100%) subsidiary of GEML; manufactures and supplies ELE-brand E-Rickshaw and E-3Wheeler parts.
- MLR Auto Limited — subsidiary: Subsidiary of GEML (67.41% holding); designs, develops, manufactures and sells L5 three-wheelers per ARAI standards.
- Excel Controlinkage Private Limited — subsidiary: Material subsidiary (80% holding, increased from 70% during the year); manufactures mechanical and electronic motion control systems, push-pull cables, levers and sensors.
- Premium Transmission Limited — related party: Fellow group company with which the Company had transactions during the year.
- Peak 15 Advisors LLP — related party: Enterprise owned or significantly influenced by Key Management Personnel.
- Pygmalion Foundation — related party: Enterprise owned or significantly influenced by Key Management Personnel.
- Greaves Limited Gratuity Fund — related party: Enterprise owned or significantly influenced by Key Management Personnel.

outlook.body:
- Under the GREAVES.NEXT strategic framework, the Company has sharpened its focus across five key business areas: Energy Solutions, Mobility Solutions, Industrial Solutions (IS), NBFC, and Technologies.
- Continued commitment to nation-building by contributing to the Government of India's 'Make in India' initiative through developing and manufacturing world-class products domestically.
- Strengthened its material subsidiary Excel Controlinkage Private Limited by acquiring an additional 10% stake (raising holding to 80%), consistent with definitive agreements signed in 2023.
- Scaling the NBFC investee business (Greaves Finance Limited) via additional equity investment to support its digital-first, EV-focused lending platform.
- The Company maintains a Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy (published on its website) governing dividend payout determinations. Its Related Party Transactions Policy was reviewed and amended by the Board on 23rd January 2025, on the Audit Committee's recommendation, to align with the SEBI (LODR) (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2024.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Greaves has allocated significant capital expenditure over the next 5-6 years for new technology development in the Auto Engines business, aimed at enhancing capabilities and meeting upcoming regulatory requirements, with growth targeted through organic expansion, contract manufacturing and deeper international market penetration. On the ESG/infrastructure side, the Company commissioned a 700 KW solar power plant at the Industrial Engines Unit, Chikalthana, Sambhajinagar, expected to generate approximately 10,02,400 units of electricity annually. Corporate-level expansion during the year included the Company increasing its stake in material subsidiary Excel Controlinkage Private Limited from 70% to 80% (12th August 2025, per definitive agreements dated 6th April 2023), and an additional equity investment of approximately Rs 22 crore in Greaves Finance Limited (GFL) completed via a rights issue on 18th September 2025 to scale its EV-focused NBFC lending platform. At the industry level, management cites data centre capacity additions targeting 3-6 GW by FY 2029-30 as a demand driver for the Energy Solutions (genset/HHP) business, though this is an industry estimate rather than a disclosed Company project.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Indian diesel generator market grew from $1.66 billion in FY25 to $1.83 billion in FY26, and is expected to expand at a CAGR of 7.18% over the next five years, reflecting sustained demand for reliable on-site power generation even as the national grid deficit narrows.
- Growth is underpinned by continued reliance on gensets in Tier II and Tier III cities, the industrial segment, data centre and telecom demand, and infrastructure/construction-sector activity that runs ahead of formal grid-connection timelines.
- By end user, the industrial segment holds a 49.02% share (process industries, warehouses, fabrication units that cannot tolerate unscheduled downtime); the commercial segment (hotels, retail chains, diagnostic labs) is upgrading to CPCB IV+ compliant models with 24/7 service contracts.
- Persistent power outage frequency in Tier II/III cities (households facing 2-4 hour daily outages despite the low national deficit) continues to drive genset demand.
- Infrastructure and real estate expansion (roads, metro, airports, industrial corridors) is creating multi-year requirements for rented 375-750 kVA generators at early-stage construction sites.
- Proliferation of telecom towers in rural and semi-urban India supports diesel genset demand where grid extension remains uneconomical.
- Adoption of rooftop solar plus battery energy storage and diesel-supply seasonality are moderating growth, though not yet displacing diesel as the primary solution for multi-hour autonomy and prime-power niches.
- India's power sector had near-475 GW capacity with the national demand-supply deficit below 1%, shifting demand emphasis toward backup and standby power systems that ensure reliability.
- Macro tailwinds cited: India GDP growth projected 6.8-7.2% for FY27, public capital expenditure of Rs 12.2 lakh crore per the Union Budget 2026-27, and rising data centre/digital infrastructure investment.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Greaves Cotton delivered record consolidated revenue of INR 3,437cr (18% YoY) and EBITDA of INR 239cr (76% YoY) driven by disciplined core business execution, with Energy Solutions growing 20% and Mobility Solutions 16%, while EV unit losses halved and international revenue rose to 13% of total — what matters is the structural margin expansion in core businesses and the path to profitability in EVs through scale and product innovation.
